_what: Close-out ledger rows that DELIBERATELY carry no CLAUDE.md §3 handoff entry, each with the reason. Asserted by scripts/verify-handoff-retention.mjs (check 5).
_the_rule_being_declared_against: A ledger row without a §3 entry is an INCOMPLETE CLOSE-OUT. §9's standing instructions say every close-out writes a §3 entry, and §3's own retention clause says a close-out that adds a FLAGGED FOR DAVID item adds a line to docs/open-questions.md too. A session that never writes a §3 entry never fires that clause either — so its flagged items reach NEITHER surface. That is why the gap is silent: it does not look like a lost entry, it looks like a session that had nothing to flag.
_why_a_declaration_and_not_a_backfill: These fifteen rows are HISTORICAL — the sessions that filed them are over, and nobody now living can write the entry they would have written. Backfilling would mean composing a handoff narrative for a session I was not in and dating it as though it had been written then, which manufactures a record rather than recovering one. Every one of these rows is COMPLETE in the ledger — the work, the SHA, the bar and the owner-proof owed are all there — so nothing is lost by declaring them; what is lost is the FLAGGED FOR DAVID items those sessions may have had, and that loss ALREADY HAPPENED and cannot be undone by inventing prose now. Declaring them says so out loud. Ledger #320.
_the_bar: An entry is admissible only if (a) the ledger row genuinely exists and is complete, and (b) the reason names what the work was, so a reader can see what §3 would have carried. A row filed FROM NOW ON does not get a declaration — it gets an entry. This list is a record of a closed gap, not a standing exemption.
_this_list_prunes_itself: The cap asserts these in the OTHER direction too: a declaration for an id with NO ledger row, or for an id that HAS since gained a §3 entry, is STALE and FAILS THE BUILD. That is deliberate, and it is tech-debt #73's lesson — verify-universals' OWNER_ONLY_PENDING is a hardcoded gap list that only grows, six of nine entries went stale, and it prints on every run, which is how a gap list stops being read. A list that cannot rot is the fix.
_derived_not_transcribed: The fifteen ids below were DERIVED, not taken from the prompt. The prompt named four (#316, #313, #311, #310) and warned that #310 and #311 appear as MENTIONS inside other entries' headings and are easy to miscount. Two independent extractions (first-id-in-heading, and ids inside the heading's first bold run excluding TECH-DEBT) agree on fifteen. #251 and #268 are NOT in this list: each is covered by a combined entry ("#250 + #251", "#267 (recon) + #268 (build)").
